The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.
SCCH 5 2.

The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 28.11.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. Anil Kumar had been riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HZ- 4206 at Rajagatta Village, Kasaba Hobli, near Anjaneya Temple, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, at that time, a driver of the Maruti Ertiga VDI Car bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MX-3293 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and all of a sudden took his vehicle to middle of the road and dashed against the said motor cycle, due to the said impact, Anil Kumar has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Taluk Government Hospital, Doddaballapura, after firstaid he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Doddaallapur, thereafter shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient.
Inspite of better treatment, Anil Kumar was succumbed to the injuries on 30.11.2022 at 10.21 a.m.
SCCH 5
The petitioners have s pent a sum of Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical treatment.

Due to head injuries, brain of the deceased was dead/dysfunctional, so Doctor's at Manipal Hospital has requested the petitioners to donate the organs of the deceased, so that, it could be saved and improved lives of needy patients who were suffering from end stage organ failure.
The petitioners being a gentleman mindset consented for organ donation and after donating organs, dead body was handed over to the petitioners.

3. At the time of accident, deceased/Anil Kumar K.R. was aged about 29 years, he was working as VMC Operator in S.K.Engineering, Peenya, Bengaluru, thereby drawing salary of Rs.23,332/- and also doing agriculture and milk vending, thereby earning Rs.35,000/- p.m.

Petitioner No.1 is mother, petitioner No.2 is father and petitioner No.3 is sister of the deceased/Anil Kumar K.R.

2 SCCH 5 petitioner No.1 is suffering from kidney stone and Doctor have fixed stent to remove kidney stone
and petitioner No.2 is suffering from arthritis and some neurological problems, have lost their bread earner of the family.

Out of the said accident, crime No.229/2022 is registerd before the Doddaballapura Rural Police against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC.
4.

It is contended that, the insured vehicle of 1 st respondent was registered earlier at Delhi dated 18.05.2012 as No.DK 09C BY 0555 with Engine No.D13A1867988 and with Chassis No.MA3FLEB1S00109898, Model Maruti Ertiga VDI, Diesel in the name of Puneet Arora, S/o.
Rakesh Arora and insured with previous insurance policy No.211200/31/2022/30167.

Further respondent No.2 has purchased the said vehicle through sale agreement SCCH 5 dated 22.04.2022 from its previous owner and thereafter respondent No.2 was applied for transfer of ownership from e a r l i e r o w n e r t o h i s n a m e o n 2 0 . 0 5 . 2 0 2 2 w i t h a p p l i c a t i o n No.KA1R220500008032/KA22052043029144 in the office of Central RTO, Bengaluru and same was transferred in the name of respondent No.2 and respondent No.2 has got certificate of registration with RC4818151 with said chassis and same engine number.

Subsequently on 20.05.2022 with effect from 21.05.2022 by respondent No.1 had issued insurance policy including previous policy No.211200/31/2022/30167 with renewed present policy No.211200/31/2023/37328 for the period from 21.05.2022 to midnight of 20.05.2023.
Hence respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with interest.

5. On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed and denied issuance policy SCCH 5 bearing No.211200/31/2023/37328 for the vehicle Maruthi Ertiga bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MX-3293.

Further submitted that, policy number mentioned by the petitioners has not been issued by this respondent and they are not the insurer to the alleged vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MX-3293.

Further denied occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained by the deceased,
treatment taken by him, age, occupation and income of the deceased.

Further submitted that,
deceased was not holding valid driving licence at the time of accident.
Respondent No.1 is entitled to take defence under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Compensation claimed by the petitioners is on higher side.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Respondent No.2/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further submitted that, respondent No.1 has SCCH 5 issued policy bearing No.21200/31/2023/37328 for the vehicle Maruthi Ertiga bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MX-3293 valid from 21.05.2022 to 20.05.2023 and policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e., 28.11.2022.
Further submitted that, previous vehicle owner by name Puneet Arora S/o. Rakesh Arora has insured with previous insurance policy No.211200/31/2022/30167 and this respondent had purchased the said vehicle through sale agreement dated 22.04.2022 from its previous ownership f r o m e a r l i e r o w n e r t o h i s n a m e o n 2 0 . 0 5 . 2 0 2 2 w i t h a p p l i c a t i o n No.KA12220500008032/KA22052043021944 in the office of Central RTO, Bengaluru and same was transferred in his name.

Further submitted that, he has got certificate or registration with RC48158151 and previous policy renewed present policy from the period 21.05.2022 to 20.05.2023,
so that, respondent No.1 cannot escape from its liability to pay compensation.

Compensation claimed by the petitioners is high, excessive, exaggerated, imaginary and unreasonable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

7. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether the petitioner proves that deceased Anil Kumar K.R. S/o.
Ramanjinappa died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 28.11.2022 at about 6.30 p.m.
when SCCH 5 deceased was riding his Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HZ- 4206 near Anjaneya Temple, Rajagatta Village, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, at that time, one Maruti Ertiga VDI Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MX-3293 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

8. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.1/mother of the deceased herself deposed her evidence as PW-1, further Accountant at S.K.Engineering is examined as PW-2 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.55 and closed his evidence.
Per contra, respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle SCCH 5 is examined as RW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.12 and closed his evidence.

9. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

Issue No.1:- In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/mother of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in her chief-examination she has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard she has exhibited copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2,
copy of further requisition of policy marked as Ex.P.3, copy of further SCCH 5 statement is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of MLC is marked as Ex.P.33, copy of P.M. Report is marked as Ex.P.34, copy of Inquest Report is marked as Ex.P.35, copy of mahazar is marked as Ex.P.36, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.37, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.38, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.55 11.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records those were marked i.e., FIR, complaint, further requisition of police, further statement, MLC, P.M.Report, inquest report, mahazar, sketch and IMV Report corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 28.11.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
12.

Per contra, respondent No.2/owner i.e., Ranganath of the offending vehicle Maruthi Ertiga bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MX-3293 has deposed his evidence as RW-1 and exhibited copy of policy marked as SCCH 5 Ex.R.1, copy of NOC marked as Ex.R.2, copy of RC marked as Ex.R.3, copy of Form No.59 marked as Ex.R.4, copy of Form No.28 marked as Ex.R.5, copy of Form No.27 marked as Ex.R.6, copy of Form No.29 and 30 marked as Ex.R.7. copy of RTO Certificates marked as Ex.R.8,
copy of RC marked as Ex.R.9, copy of Aadhar Card marked as Ex.R.10, copy of DL marked as Ex.R.11 and copy of RC marked as Ex.R.12.
13. Further respondent No.2 who being the R.C.Owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-MX-3293 is examined as RW-1.

In his evidence he has categorically admitted about purchase of vehicle from one Puneet Arora i.e., previously the said vehicle was registered at Delhi and insurance policy renewed from 21.05.2022 to 20.05.2023 and after purchase, the old number has been converted into new No.KA-01-MX-3293 in his name and for the date of the accident i.e., on SCCH 5 28.11.2022, insurance policy is in force etc.,
To support his case, he has exhibited Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.12 documents, that too, the said documents already marked by the petitioner on behalf of him.

So on perusal of the documents marked by the RW-1, they are cover note, insurance certificate cum policy schedule, in the said documents they have mentioned vehicle registration No.DL09CBY0555 and Engine No. & Chassis No.D13A1867988, MA3FLEB1S00109898 in the name of Puneet Arora and valid from 21.05.2022 to midnight 20.05.2023.
RW-1 has also exhibited Ex.R.2 Cover Note, Ex.R.3 is copy of Registration Certificate of Puneet Arora pertaining to vehicle No.DL-9C-BY-0555.

He also exhibited Ex.R.4 which is Form No.59, Ex.R.5 Form No.28, which is in the name of Ranganath i.e.,
2nd respondent, that means, the said old number is Delhi registration vehicle, which has been transferred from SCCH 5 Puneet Arora name to Ranganath.

Further he also exhibited Ex.R.6 i.e.,
Form No.27 and said document also corroborates the fact of the petitioner that, the previous old DL bearing No.DL9CBY0555 car had insurance policy with respondent No.1 for the date of the alleged accident and said vehicle has been transferred to the name of the respondent No.2 bearing Karnataka registration No.KA- 01-MX-3293, but in all documents and evidence of RW-1, the registration number tally with each other including policy i.e., Ex.R.1 and other documents.

So the said documents further clarifies to the court about having of the policy to the offending vehicle for the date of the alleged accident.
Further admittedly except filing written statement, SCCH 5 respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence to substantiate the written statement contents.

15. Further except oral evidence of respondent No.1, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of Anil Kumar K.R. out of the accident held on 28.11.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. when he was riding Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HZ-4206 at Rajagatta Village, Kasaba Hobli, near Anjaneya Temple, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
SCCH 5 16.
The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the Maruthi Ertiga VDI Car bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MX-3293.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Anil Kumar K.R. was aged about 29 years as on the date of accident.

For proof of age of the deceased, they have produced copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.5, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 30.08.1993, the alleged accident was occurred on 28.11.2022.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.5, age of the deceased is considered about 30 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 17 is applicable SCCH 5 with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

Peenya, Bengaluru and drawing salary of Rs.23,332/- p.m. and he is also doing agriculture and milk vending, thereby earning Rs.35,000/- p.m.

To prove the same, petitioners have exhibited copy of payslips marked as Ex.P.12, copy of account extract marked as Ex.P.13.
19.

as PW-2 and got marked authorization letter marked as Ex.P.42, copy of ID card marked as Ex.P.43,

Further on perusal of Ex.P.45 and Ex.P.46 payslips and attendance register of the deceased Anil Kumar K.R. including Ex.P.50 appointment letter and evidence PW-2 Sri.Ramesha S. clearly indicates to the court that, deceased Anil Kumar, who was working in the company of PW-2 i.e.,
S.K.Engineering and he was getting salary of Rs.21,044/- in the month of October 2022 and Rs.24,757/- in the month of November 2022, that means in the alleged accident month itself,
deceased SCCH 5 Anilkumar was got the salary of Rs.24,757/-.

Contradictory to the said materials,
except cross- examination by respondent No.1 and 2, they have not placed any other materials nor disproved with regard to the avocation of the deceased Anil Kumar.
So in the absence of rebuttal evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the evidence of PW-2, who is employer of S.K.Engineering.

The documents those have marked in this case with regard to occupation of the deceased Anil Kumar with S.K.Engineering, that means, PW-2 is employer of the S.K.Engineering has exhibited Ex.P.42 to Ex.P.46 documents, said documents corroborates the case of the petitioners that,
deceased Anil Kumar was ITI Graduate and was working in said S.K.Engineering and he was getting regular salary or permanent salary in the said company.

Accordingly as per Ex.P.46 payslip for the month of November 2022, notional income of the SCCH 5 deceased Anil Kumar is taken into consideration i.e., a sum of Rs.24,757/- for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.
21. Further petitioner No.1 is mother, petitioner No.2 is father and petitioner No.3 is sister of the deceased/Anil Kumar K.R.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar card of petitioner No.1 to 3 marked as Ex.P.5 it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased/Anil Kumar K.R. hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

22. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased is bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

23. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s.
SCCH 5 Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case of fixed salary employee.

In the case on hand, the monthly income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.xxxx/- p.m. hence,
which is taken for additional weightage at the rate of 40% with reference to his age.
24. Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

Sl. Particulars Calculation Total No.
 (i) Monthly Income Rs.24,757/-
(ii) 40% of (i) above if Rs.24,757/- (+) added to the Rs.9,903/- = monthly income as Rs.34,660/-

Further petitioner No.1 and 2 being the parents, petitioner No.3 being the sister of the deceased are entitled for Rs.20,000/- each towards filial consortium.
Further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.
26. Further petitioners have exhibited medical bills to the tune of Rs.3,18,216/- marked as Ex.P.7.

On perusal of the said medical bills it is noticed that, out of final bill of Rs.2,15,244/-, a deposit receipt for a sum of Rs.1,500/-, Rs.50,000/-, Rs.1,63,744/- along with a bill of Rs.9,616/- is furnished.
So petitioners are entitled for Rs.2,24,860/-.
Further they have also produced a 2 bills for Rs.1,500/- and Rs.50,000/-, which cannot be taken SCCH 5 into consideration for the calculation of medical bills.

Further petitioners have exhibited case sheet pertaining to deceased marked as Ex.P.20.
27.

Petitioners in claim petition have contended that, due to disfunction of brain of the deceased, as per the suggestions of the Doctors, they have donated the organs of the deceased, which could be saved and improved lives of needy patients who were suffering from end stage of organ failure,
despite deep pain and sorrow suffered by them.

In this regard, they have exhibited copy of eye donation certificate marked as Ex.P.14, copy of acknowledgment marked as Ex.P.15, copy of appreciation letters marked as Ex.P.16.
28.

Petitioners have contended in the claim petition that, petitioner No.1 being the mother of the deceased was diagnosed with kidney infection and suffering from kidney stone and she has been under SCCH 5 treatment under kidneyt stone and petitioner No.2 being the father of the deceased is suffering from arthritis and some neurological problems.

In this regard, they have exhibited medial bills of Rs.1,49,836/- pertaining to petitioner No.1 marked as Ex.P.18, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.19 and case sheet pertaining to petitioner No.1 marked as Ex.P.21.
On perusal of these medical records and medical bills it is noticed that, the expenses incurred by the petitioners on 28.09.2021 which is prior to the date of accident i.e., 28.11.2022.
So these medical bills are not taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of compensation.

3. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 4.
Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 5.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.38,50,180/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

31. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer of the Maruti Ertiga VDI Car bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-MX-3293 has issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 vide policy bearing No.211200/31/2023/37328, which is disputed by the respondent No.1 in the written statement.
As discussed above, respondent No.1 being the insurer is directed deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of SCCH 5 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.38,50,180/- (Rupees Thirty Eight Lakhs Fifty Thousand One Hundred Eighty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 45:45:10 in the award amount.

SCCH 5 The petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
: 
The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.
Inspite of better treatment, Anil Kumar was succumbed to the injuries on 30.11.2022 at 10.21 a.m.
Due to head injuries, brain of the deceased was dead/dysfunctional, so Doctor's at Manipal Hospital has requested the petitioners to donate the organs of the deceased, so that, it could be saved and improved lives of needy patients who were suffering from end stage organ failure.
The petitioners being a gentleman mindset consented for organ donation and after donating organs, dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Out of the said accident, crime No.229/2022 is registerd before the Doddaballapura Rural Police against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC.
4.
It is contended that, the insured vehicle of 1 st respondent was registered earlier at Delhi dated 18.05.2012 as No.DK 09C BY 0555 with Engine No.D13A1867988 and with Chassis No.MA3FLEB1S00109898, Model Maruti Ertiga VDI, Diesel in the name of Puneet Arora, S/o.
Rakesh Arora and insured with previous insurance policy No.211200/31/2022/30167.
Subsequently on 20.05.2022 with effect from 21.05.2022 by respondent No.1 had issued insurance policy including previous policy No.211200/31/2022/30167 with renewed present policy No.211200/31/2023/37328 for the period from 21.05.2022 to midnight of 20.05.2023.
Hence respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with interest.
Further denied occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained by the deceased,
treatment taken by him, age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Further submitted that,
deceased was not holding valid driving licence at the time of accident.
Respondent No.1 is entitled to take defence under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Compensation claimed by the petitioners is on higher side.
Further submitted that, he has got certificate or registration with RC48158151 and previous policy renewed present policy from the period 21.05.2022 to 20.05.2023,
so that, respondent No.1 cannot escape from its liability to pay compensation.

opennyai_summary.issue:
7. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether the petitioner proves that deceased Anil Kumar K.R. S/o.
Ramanjinappa died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 28.11.2022 at about 6.30 p.m.
when SCCH 5 deceased was riding his Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HZ- 4206 near Anjaneya Temple, Rajagatta Village, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, at that time, one Maruti Ertiga VDI Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MX-3293 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.5, age of the deceased is considered about 30 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 17 is applicable SCCH 5 with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

V/s.
SCCH 5 Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case of fixed salary employee.

::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.38,50,180/- (Rupees Thirty Eight Lakhs Fifty Thousand One Hundred Eighty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

SCCH 5 The petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
